extracted.intended_audience: agency heads, program managers, accessibility/compliance officers, and legal staff responsible for implementing section 504 obligations in Federal agencies (e.g., National Capital Planning Commission)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements that Executive agencies must follow to prohibit discrimination on the basis of handicap, ensure program accessibility, provide effective communications, conduct self-evaluations, and process complaints under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging interest on unpaid bills (FOIA fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may charge interest on any unpaid bill starting on the 31st day following the date of billing the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest assessed at the rate provided in 31 U.S.C. 3717 and will accrue from the billing date until payment is received. The Commission will follow the Debt Collection Act of 1982 and its administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregating requests to prevent fee avoidance (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission reasonably determines that a requester or group acting together is attempting to divide a request into a series of requests for the purpose of avoiding fees, the Commission may aggregate those requests and charge accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may presume multiple requests involving related matters submitted within a 30 calendar day period were made to avoid fees. For requests separated by a longer period, aggregation requires a reasonable basis in view of all circumstances. The Commission shall not aggregate multiple requests involving unrelated matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutorily-based fee schedules override general FOIA fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee schedule of this section does not apply to fees charged under any statute that specifically requires an agency to set and collect fees for particular types of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When records responsive to a request are subject to a statutorily-based fee schedule program, the Commission must inform the requester of the contact information for that program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the regulation (Part 457/500)
rubrics_metrics.description: This part effectuates section 119 of the Rehabilitation Amendments of 1978, which amended section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 to prohibit discrimination on the basis of handicap in programs or activities conducted by Executive agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: scope of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: This part applies to all programs or activities conducted by the agency (Executive agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: as used in this part, section 504 applies only to programs or activities conducted by Executive agencies and not to federally assisted programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: 'auxiliary aids'
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary aids means services or devices that enable persons with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills to have an equal opportunity to participate in, and enjoy the benefits of, programs or activities conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for persons with impaired vision — readers, brailled materials, audio recordings, telecommunications devices; for persons with impaired hearing — telephone handset amplifiers, telephones compatible with hearing aids, TDDs, interpreters, notetakers, written materials. The agency shall give primary consideration to the requests of the handicapped person in determining the type of aid necessary. The agency need not provide individually prescribed devices, readers for personal use or study, or other devices of a personal nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: 'complete complaint'
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete complaint is a written statement that contains the complainant’s name and address and describes the agency’s alleged discriminatory action in sufficient detail to inform the agency of the nature and date of the alleged violation of section 504, and is signed by the complainant or an authorized representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints filed on behalf of classes or third parties shall describe or identify (by name, if possible) the alleged victims of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: 'handicapped person' and related subcriteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Handicapped person means any person who has a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, has a record of such an impairment, or is regarded as having such an impairment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical or mental impairment includes a broad list of physiological disorders, mental or psychological disorders, and specific diseases (examples provided). Major life activities include caring for oneself, performing manual tasks, walking, seeing, hearing, speaking, breathing, learning, and working. 'Has a record' means history or misclassification. 'Is regarded as' has three illustrative sub-conditions (treated as having limitation, limited due to others' attitudes, or treated as having impairment though none exists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: 'qualified handicapped person'
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified handicapped person means—(1) for preschool/elementary/secondary education: a handicapped person who is a member of a class otherwise entitled to receive education services; (2) for programs requiring performance/accomplishment: someone who meets essential eligibility requirements and can achieve purpose without modifications that would fundamentally alter the program; (3) for other programs: someone who meets essential eligibility requirements for participation or receipt of benefits; (4) for employment: as defined in 29 CFR 1613.702(f) and applied by § 457.140.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-evaluation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall, by August 24, 1987, evaluate its current policies and practices, and the effects thereof, that do not or may not meet the requirements of this part, and, to the extent modification is required, proceed to make the necessary modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency shall provide an opportunity for interested persons, including handicapped persons or organizations representing them, to participate in the self-evaluation process by submitting comments (oral and written). The agency shall maintain on file and make available for public inspection for three years a description of areas examined and any problems identified, and a description of any modifications made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall make available to employees, applicants, participants, beneficiaries, and other interested persons such information regarding the provisions of this part and its applicability to the programs or activities conducted by the agency, and make such information available in such manner as the head of the agency finds necessary to apprise such persons of the protections assured by section 504 and this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibitions: no exclusion or denial on basis of handicap
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibitions in provision of aid/benefit/service (specific prohibitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In providing any aid, benefit, or service the agency may not, directly or through contractual, licensing, or other arrangements, on the basis of handicap: (i) deny a qualified handicapped person the opportunity to participate in or benefit from the aid/benefit/service; (ii) afford an opportunity that is not equal to that afforded others; (iii) provide an aid/benefit/service that is not as effective in affording equal opportunity to obtain the same result/benefit/achievement; (iv) provide different or separate aids unless necessary to provide equally effective opportunities; (v) deny opportunity to participate as a member of planning or advisory boards; (vi) otherwise limit enjoyment of any right, privilege, advantage, or opportunity enjoyed by others receiving the aid/benefit/service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory methods of administration and site selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not, directly or through contractual or other arrangements, utilize criteria or methods of administration that (i) subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap; or (ii) defeat or substantially impair accomplishment of the objectives of a program or activity with respect to handicapped persons. In selecting site or location of a facility, the agency may not make selections the purpose or effect of which would exclude handicapped persons or defeat/objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement and licensing: non-discrimination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency, in the selection of procurement contractors, may not use criteria that subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination. The agency may not administer a licensing or certification program in a manner that subjects qualified handicapped persons to discrimination, nor establish requirements for licensees or certified entities that do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs or activities of entities licensed or certified by the agency are not themselves covered by this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated setting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall administer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified handicapped persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility — general standard for existing facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall operate each program or activity so that the program or activity, when viewed in its entirety, is readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not necessarily require each existing facility to be accessible, and exceptions exist for historic preservation programs and where compliance would result in a fundamental alteration or undue financial and administrative burdens (agency bears burden to prove and must issue written statement). Where such alteration or burden would result, the agency must take other actions that would not cause such alteration/burdens but would ensure that handicapped persons receive the benefits/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility — acceptable methods for compliance (existing facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may comply by redesign of equipment, reassignment of services to accessible buildings, assignment of aides to beneficiaries, home visits, delivery of services at alternate accessible sites, alteration of existing facilities and construction of new facilities, use of accessible rolling stock, or any other methods that result in readily accessible programs/activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency is not required to make structural changes where other methods are effective. In choosing among methods, agency shall give priority to those that offer programs/activities to qualified handicapped persons in the most integrated setting appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility — historic preservation exception and preferred methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In historic preservation programs, the agency shall give priority to methods that provide physical access to handicapped persons, but where physical alteration is not required because of historic considerations or fundamental alteration/undue burden exceptions, acceptable alternative methods include audio-visual materials/devices to depict inaccessible portions, assigning persons to guide handicapped persons through portions that cannot be made accessible, or adopting other innovative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial impairment is defined as significant loss of integrity of finished materials, design quality, or special character resulting from a permanent alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility — time periods for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall comply with obligations under § 457.150 by October 21, 1986; where structural changes are undertaken, such changes shall be made by August 22, 1989, but in any event as expeditiously as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where structural changes will be undertaken to achieve program accessibility, the agency shall develop by February 23, 1987 a transition plan setting forth the steps necessary to complete such changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transition plan shall: (1) identify physical obstacles in the agency's facilities that limit accessibility; (2) describe in detail methods to be used to make facilities accessible; (3) specify the schedule for taking steps necessary to achieve compliance and, if longer than one year, identify steps for each year of the transition period; (4) indicate the official responsible for implementation. The agency shall provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons/orgs) to participate in development of the transition plan by submitting comments and shall make a copy available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: New construction and alterations standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Each building or part of a building constructed or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of the agency shall be designed, constructed, or altered so as to be readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definitions, requirements, and standards of the Architectural Barriers Act (42 U.S.C. 4151–4157), as established in 41 CFR 101–19.600 to 101–19.607, apply to buildings covered by this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications: effective communication and auxiliary aids
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure effective communication with applicants, participants, personnel of other Federal entities, and members of the public, and shall furnish appropriate auxiliary aids where necessary to afford a handicapped person an equal opportunity to participate in and enjoy the benefits of a program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary consideration shall be given to the requests of the handicapped person when determining type of auxiliary aid. Agency need not provide individually prescribed devices, readers for personal use or study, or devices of a personal nature. Where communicating by telephone, TDDs or equally effective systems shall be used. The agency shall ensure persons with impaired vision or hearing can obtain information as to existence and location of accessible services and facilities. The agency shall provide signage at a primary entrance to inaccessible facilities directing users to where they can obtain information about accessible facilities; the international symbol for accessibility shall be used at each primary entrance of an accessible facility. The section does not require actions that would result in fundamental alteration or undue financial/administrative burdens; agency has burden to prove and must provide written statement. If such alteration/burdens would result, the agency shall take other actions that would not result in such alteration/burdens but would, to the maximum extent possible, ensure that handicapped persons receive benefits/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance procedures — coverage and delegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Section applies to all allegations of discrimination on basis of handicap in programs/activities conducted by the agency except that employment complaints are processed according to EEOC procedures (29 CFR part 1613). The Executive Director is responsible for coordinating implementation. The agency may delegate authority for conducting complaint investigations to other Federal agencies, except the authority for making the final determination may not be delegated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints may be sent to the agency's Equal Employment Opportunity Director (address given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint filing deadlines and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: All complete complaints must be filed within 180 days of the alleged act of discrimination. The agency may extend this time period for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency receives a complaint over which it does not have jurisdiction, it shall promptly notify the complainant and make reasonable efforts to refer the complaint to the appropriate government entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural/ATBCB notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall notify the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board upon receipt of any complaint alleging that a building or facility subject to the Architectural Barriers Act or section 502 of the Rehabilitation Act is not readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation result timelines and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days of receipt of a complete complaint for which it has jurisdiction, the agency shall notify the complainant of the results of the investigation in a letter containing (1) findings of fact and conclusions of law; (2) a description of a remedy for each violation found; and (3) a notice of the right to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals procedures and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals of findings of fact and conclusions of law or remedies must be filed by the complainant within 90 days of receipt from the agency of the letter required by § 457.170(g). Timely appeals shall be accepted and processed by the head of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The head of the agency shall notify the complainant of the results of the appeal within 60 days of receipt of the request. If additional information is needed from the complainant, the head has 60 days from receipt of the additional information to make a determination. The time limits in paragraphs (g) and (j) may be extended with the permission of the Assistant Attorney General.
